question: The glass electrode combined with a reference electrode is the most used device for measuring the pH of a solution and is characterized in that:

options.opa: It responds to the concentration of hydrogen bonds in the solution.
options.opb: It responds to the hydrogen ion activity in the solution.
options.opc: No calibration needed with standard buffers (patterns)
options.opd: When very alkaline solutions with high concentrations of sodium ions are available, when performing the pH measurements, the electrode never presents any interference.
